title: A Write-Off Approved Before the Controller Limit Dropped
scenario_text:
A finance analyst at Wardlow Networks must confirm the required approval for a bad-debt write-off, given how a similar write-off was handled earlier this year.

**Decision A (2024-02)**
An $18,000 bad-debt write-off was approved by the Controller alone. Note: 'Under the delegation of authority then in effect, the Controller could approve write-offs up to $25,000 without CFO involvement.'

**Current request C (2024-07-10)**
An $18,000 bad-debt write-off is proposed for an uncollectible customer balance. The AR manager wants the Controller to approve it solo, the same way the February write-off was handled.

**Delegation of Authority Policy (current, effective 2024-05-01)**
The Controller may approve bad-debt write-offs up to $10,000 without further sign-off. Write-offs above $10,000 now require CFO approval. The prior Controller limit of $25,000 was lowered to $10,000 when this policy took effect on May 1, 2024.

**Slack — #finance-ops**
AR mgr: 'The Controller approved an $18K write-off solo back in February — no issue. Let's just have her sign this one the same way.'
Analyst: 'February was before the May delegation change. The Controller's limit dropped to $10K. Let me confirm who has to approve $18K now.'

The AR manager is treating the February approval as proof the Controller can act alone at this amount. The write-off has not yet been routed to the CFO.
question: Whose approval is required for the $18,000 bad-debt write-off under the current policy?
